description.narrative:
Strengthening Regional Platforms for a Strong and Inclusive National Climate Movement in Burkina Faso
Through the African Activists for Climate Justice (AACJ) program, large-scale actions were carried out between 2021 and 2024 to strengthen the capacities of CSOs, raise awareness among communities, and convey messages to decision-makers. However, despite these achievements, climate movementsin Burkina Faso remain insufficiently structured, particularly at the regional level, which limits their collective effectiveness and their capacity for national influence.
Currently, most actions are carried out by central organizations, mainly based in the capital Ouagadougou, with little coordination and structuring at the level of the country's 13 regions. However, climate realities and vulnerabilities differ from one region to another, and it is essential that movements be rooted locally to capture specific needs, mobilize communities, and put forward demands rooted in the territories. Regional structuringwould also create a bottom-up dynamic tofuel national and international advocacy with concrete data and testimonies from the field. In this context, targeted action to structure climate movements from the regional to the national level appears crucial.It will help to unite initiatives, foster synergiesbetween local and national actors, and give greater coherence and strength to advocacy and mobilization actions. It will also strengthen local leadership (particularly of youth and women) in the climatemovement, in accordance with the principles of inclusion and social justice.
General objective: Strengthen the structuring of climate movements in the 13 regions of Burkina Faso in order to consolidate their coordination at the national level for greatereffectiveness in the fight for climate justice. Specific objectives: Establish an operational national coordination structure for climate movements

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Intermón is since 1997 a member of the international Oxfam confederation, sharing values and a strategic plan to achieve greater global impact. Intermón Oxfam fights, with and for disadvantaged populations and as part of a broad global movement, with the aim of eradicating injustice and poverty, and to ensure that all human beings can fully exercise their rights and enjoy a dignified life. Mission, Vision and Values are the components of Oxfam Intermón identity and guide its steps as an organisation and the ideal with which Oxfam Intermón wants to live in order to obtain a fairer world with greater solidarity.

description.narrative: CSOs have strengthened capacity (and maintain and expand their civic space) to engage local, nationally and internationally in influencing on gendered climate justice, natural resources and/or land rights issues in an effective and inclusive way.
CSOs who demonstrate strengthened capacity to engage in influencing

comment.narrative: The intervention strengthened the capacity of civil society organisations (CSOs) to engage in influencing by reinforcing coordination, collective organisation, and strategic alignment of climate movements across the 13 regions of Burkina Faso. A rapid mapping of regional climate actors improved visibility of engaged CSOs, youth and women’s groups, and community leaders, while a national structuring process enabled regional representatives to jointly define a shared vision and governance framework througha validated national charter. This strengthened internal cohesion, clarified roles, and enhanced the legitimacy of the movement as a coordinated national actor, which was further demonstrated through collective engagement in a national climate campaign. Ongoing coordination between regional and national levels was sustained through a simple digital communication mechanism, enabling CSOs to align positions, mobilise collectively, and engage more effectively in national climate justice influencing.
